Math / Percentage

Percentage Calculator

Solve the three common percentage questions: find a percentage of a number, determine what percent one amount is of another, or find the percentage change between two values. Each mode uses a clearly defined base to avoid confusing percentage points with percent change. Choose the relationship you know. “P% of X” is X × P/100; “A is what percent of B” is A/B × 100; percent change is (new − old)/|old| × 100.

How to use this calculator

  1. Enter question, percent or first value, base or second value.
  2. Select Calculate to see the answer and its breakdown.
  3. Keep a scenario, change an input and compare the results.

Use consistent units and check the assumptions below before applying the result.

How percentage is calculated

Choose the relationship you know. “P% of X” is X × P/100; “A is what percent of B” is A/B × 100; percent change is (new − old)/|old| × 100. A price moving from 80 to 92 changes by (92−80)/80 × 100 = 15%.

Percent of: P×X/100; part as percent: A/B×100; percent change: (new−old)/|old|×100.
A worked example

A price moving from 80 to 92 changes by (92−80)/80 × 100 = 15%.

Assumptions & useful context

The result depends on the values you enter and the method described above. Displayed numbers may be rounded; calculations use the unrounded values. Check that this model matches your situation before relying on it.

Frequently asked questions

What does a negative change mean?

The new value is below the starting value; the signed result preserves that direction.

Why can percent change be undefined?

A zero starting value cannot serve as the denominator.
